plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $31, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $31, ensuring I maximize expected profit without risk of overpaying.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid up or down. I will bid my true value of $31.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so there's no benefit to shading your bid. Bidding exactly my value of $46 maximizes my expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I pay only that competing bid, ensuring I never pay more than my value and always capture positive surplus when I win.
